summary: Johannes Rahder was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology who earned his doctorate from Utrecht University. He held chairs at Utrecht (1930–1931) and Leiden (1931–1946) before serving as a professor at Yale University (1947–1965).

Johannes Schmidt worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Bonn, Jena, and under August Schleicher and Albrecht Weber. He held professorial posts at the University of Bonn (1868), University of Graz (1873–1876), and Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1876).

Johannes Schneider is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Marburg. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin, the University of Munich, and the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Johannes Schubert specialized in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at Leipzig University and under August Conrady and Friedrich Weller. He worked at the Leipzig University Library (ca. 1927–1954) and held teaching posts and a professorship at Leipzig University (1934–1962).

John A. Ardussi is a historian and Tibetologist who studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie and earned his PhD from Australian National University (attested 1977). He has served as a research team member at the CNRS.

John Alexander Stewart, an Aberdeen graduate who worked in linguistics, served in the Indian Civil Service from ca. 1905 to 1933. From ca. 1933 to 1948, he held posts as Reader in Burmese at the University of London and SOAS.

John Allan worked in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at Edinburgh and Leipzig. He was Keeper of Coins and Medals at the British Museum (1931) and lectured in Sanskrit at UCL (1907–1917), SOAS (1920–1922), and Edinburgh (1949–1955).

John Avery was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Amherst, Tübingen, Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney. He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).

John B. Cobb Jr. is a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago and founded the Center for Process Studies. He was attested in 1989 holding professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University.
John Berthrong was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under graduate supervisor Alfonso Verdu. He held a post at Boston University from ca. 1989 to 2013.

John Borthwick Gilchrist was an Indologist and linguist educated at Edinburgh. He served as principal of Fort William College (1800–1804), Oriental Professor at East India Company College (1806), and first Professor of Hindustani at University College London (ca. 1828–1831).
John Bray is a researcher in Tibetology and history/archaeology who studied under Tsering Dhundup Gonkatsang. He has held a post at the International Association for Ladakh Studies.
John Brockington is an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Edinburgh, with his affiliation attested in 1987 and 2003.

John Brough, an Indologist and linguist, studied at Edinburgh and Cambridge under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Harold Walter Bailey. He held chairs as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1948–1967) and professor at the University of Cambridge (1967–1984).
John Buescher is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982. He served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

John Burnet was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a long-standing academic post at the University of St Andrews from ca. 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page worked in Indology and history/archaeology, having studied at Oxford and the Royal College of Music. He held posts at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (ca. 1950–1953) and SOAS University of London (ca. 1953–1984).
John C. Huntington was a scholar in history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University, where his tenure was attested in 1987–1990 and 2000.

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served on the faculty at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy in 2015.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classicist educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked at the University of Oxford (ca. 1946–1952) and Cambridge, where he served as Perceval Maitland Laurence Reader in Classics from 1969 to 1984.
